title: Temporal burst mitigator and quantile-consensus rollout guard
author: Priya Menon
body:
Motivation: Canary detectors today are sensitive to short-lived traffic bursts and noisy tail samples across shards. This leads to false positives during ephemeral load spikes and excessive rollbacks. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: (1) Temporal Burst Mitigator (TBM) — a lightweight traffic-smoothing preprocessor that normalizes short-term burstiness before metrics are fed into detectors; (2) Quantile Consensus Guard (QCG) — a guard that fuses quantile estimates from multiple execution shards/nodes using a robust consensus algorithm to reduce false alarms from localized tail noise.

What this change does: Implements TBM as a pluggable preprocessing stage in the canary ingestion pipeline; TBM computes an exponential moving average of arrival rates and applies a short sliding-window dampening factor to limit spiky contributions to latency percentiles. QCG computes a consensus range for a configured set of quantiles (p50, p95, p99) using median-of-means and an outlier-trim step; the canary evaluator only triggers if the consensus indicates a regression across a quorum of shards.

Design highlights: - TBM parameters (window_ms, smoothing_alpha, burst_threshold) are configurable per canary config; defaults chosen to be conservative for general traffic patterns. - QCG exposes quorum_size and trim_fraction; defaults: quorum = 0.66 of reporting shards, trim_fraction = 0.15. - Integrates with existing canary backoff/rollback logic: QCG is a precondition check to prevent noisy single-shard regressions from failing a rollout. - Adds telemetry: tbm.bursts_suppressed, qcg.quorum_failures, qcg.consensus_width, and per-quantile consensus values.

Compatibility and rollout strategy: Both features are opt-in behind canary config flags. Default config enables QCG for any canary with >3 shards and TBM for canaries with 1k+ qps by default; these defaults can be overridden via canary policy. We will gate full platform rollout for 2 weeks in the staging/perf ring and ingest metrics into a new observability dashboard.

Testing: - Unit tests for TBM smoothing math and boundary conditions (zero traffic, constant load, burst windows). - Unit tests for QCG consensus logic with synthetic shard samples (including adversarial shards). - Integration test: end-to-end canary run in perf-sim harness under simulated burst traffic shows TBM prevents false-positive rollback in 94/100 runs. - Canary lab run against production traffic shape (shadowed) for 48h.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation of TBM and QCG algorithms - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests in perf-sim harness - [x] New metrics emitted and documented - [x] Documentation changes for canary config (values.yaml defaults updated) - [x] Feature gated and staged rollout plan

Commits summary:  - feat(tbm): add temporal burst mitigator preprocessing stage and API hooks  - feat(qcg): add quantile consensus guard and quorum logic  - test: add unit/integration tests and perf-sim scenarios  - docs: document configuration and metrics  - ci: add small perf job to CI that runs TBM/QCG sanity checks

Files changed (high level): src/detectors/temporal_burst_mitigator.py, src/rollout/quantile_consensus_guard.go, src/canary/config.go, charts/perf-canary/values.yaml, tests/perf/tbm_qcg_integration_test.py, docs/canary/guards.md, .github/workflows/perf-check.yml

Notes: The body text contains choices (median-of-means, trim fraction, smoothing) with brief rationale; these hyperparameters are set conservatively and exposed for tuning.

review_comments: Aisha Khan: Please add a short section in docs explaining how smoothing interacts with request batching and KV cache—could smoothing mask real latency regressions for bursty but valid workload patterns?
Priya Menon: Good point — added docs note and a unit test that asserts no suppression for uniformly higher latency across the window.
Diego Rivera: The quorum threshold default (0.66) seems arbitrary; can we justify with empirical results? Also include fallback if only 2 shards are reporting.
Priya Menon: Added a small experiment summary in docs (see tests/perf/consensus_experiment.md) and fallback logic to require simple majority if shards <4.
Benji Lee: CI showed a flaky integration test in the first run (random seed causing one failure). Can we make the test deterministic or retry in CI?
Priya Menon: Made tests deterministic by fixing RNG seeds and added a retry wrapper for the perf-check job; reran CI and all checks passed.
ci_log: Checks: build (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-perf (pass after retry), lint (pass), perf-check (pass). Note: perf-check was flaky on first run due to non-deterministic seed; fixed and reran.
release_notes: Added Temporal Burst Mitigator to smooth short-lived arrival spikes before detection, and Quantile Consensus Guard to reduce false positives from shard-local tail noise; opt-in via canary config with conservative defaults. Expect reduced noisy rollbacks for bursty traffic patterns.
